oneLiner: Closed at 7,580.07 Friday, down 1.82% on the day and about 0.6% on the week, roughly 3.1% below the record close of 7,818.93 set on October 6.
intro: The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07 on Friday, October 30, down 1.82% on the day and about 0.6% on the week, its third straight weekly decline. That leaves the index roughly 3.1% below its record close of 7,818.93 from October 6. Worries about heavy AI spending, after disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel, drove the late-week slide.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above shows SPY slipping again this week, with the biggest damage on Friday. The index itself lost about 0.6% over the five sessions, its third weekly decline in a row, as a technology-led slide on Thursday and Friday followed Wednesday's Fed hold. SPY's figures on the cards may differ slightly from the index numbers here.

chart.heading: The trend against its moving averages
chart.body: The index has drifted away from its October 6 record over several weeks, a pattern chart watchers often track. The chart above plots SPY against its own moving-average lines over the same stretch, so the exact positions there may differ a little from the index figures quoted here. Friday's drop was the index's sharpest since June.

levels.heading: Where the nearby levels sit
levels.body: The October 6 record close of 7,818.93 is the nearest marker above, the same roughly 3.1% gap noted at the top of the page. Below, the index's recent trading range may be what watchers look at next. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where those levels sit on SPY today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: Momentum weakened as the index gave back ground late in the week, with chip stocks and other AI-linked shares leading the slide. Nvidia was the heaviest single drag on Friday. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on SPY, which may help show how far that momentum has faded.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 0.6% this week, its third straight weekly loss, and it now sits roughly 3.1% under its record. Friday's 1.82% drop was the index's worst day since June.

marketRead: The S&P 500 ended the week at 7,580.07, down about 0.6% and roughly 3.1% below its October 6 record close of 7,818.93. The first half of the week was quieter. On Wednesday, October 28, the Federal Reserve left its policy rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two officials preferring a quarter-point rise. The mood turned on Thursday, when Alphabet fell more than 12%, its worst day on record, after reporting heavy AI-related spending and cash burn.

Friday, October 30, brought the sharpest damage. The index fell 1.82%, its worst day since June, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.86%. Intel plunged 28.6% after a weak revenue outlook and a cash-burn warning, Nvidia fell 4.2%, and Amazon's heavy cash outflow added to the worry, reviving doubts about whether huge AI spending will pay off. The Dow fell a smaller 1.09% and some sectors outside technology held up better.

Rates offered some relief. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.9% on Friday, after trading above 5.30% earlier in October. Even so, markets still leaned toward tightening: CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point rise at the December 9 meeting above 80% on October 28, around the time of the decision. Oil stayed high, with WTI crude settling at about $104 a barrel, which may keep inflation worries alive.

About 59% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average and 61% above their 50-day average at Friday's close, according to ChartRow. The optimistic case is that yields have eased and some sectors outside technology held up. The cautious case is that three straight weekly losses, possible further rate rises and doubts over AI returns could keep leadership fragile. The coming weeks may hinge on remaining big-company earnings, inflation data and the Fed's December meeting.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: AI-spending worries after Alphabet, Amazon and Intel results drove a Thursday-Friday slide; Friday was the worst day since June.

points.label: Breadth
points.text: About 59% of S&P 500 members were above their 200-day average at Friday's close, and 61% above their 50-day average.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The 10-year yield was near 4.9% on Friday; the Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote on October 28.

watchDown: The index extends its three-week slide and moves further from the October 6 record close of 7,818.93.
AI-linked technology shares keep falling as investors question heavy spending by Alphabet, Amazon and others.
Rate-rise bets build again, pushing Treasury yields back toward the 5% area.
Oil prices climb further, keeping inflation worries and Treasury yields elevated.
watchUp: The index recovers this week's losses and heads back toward the October 6 record close of 7,818.93.
The 10-year Treasury yield keeps easing from about 4.9% as rate-rise bets cool.
Upcoming company earnings show AI spending paying off, calming this week's valuation worries.
Breadth holds near 60% of members above their 200-day average even as technology wobbles.
